sam.belief: I saw a tall shape beside Reservoir Road after my bus route, in poor visibility. I cannot say what it was; I remain the only one claiming a sighting.
sam.stance: I stand by Reservoir Road Tall because it records the place and what I could make out. Harold and Ellen have never seen it, and their proposals do not change my account.

harold.belief: I have only Sam's account. I have never seen the shape, and I am not convinced Sam can identify what he saw.
harold.stance: I stand by Roadside Figure: it is concise and does not claim to settle what Sam saw. I still prefer it to a name tied too closely to one report.

ellen.belief: I have never seen it. A report of a tall shape is not enough to establish what it was.
ellen.stance: I stand by Unidentified Tall Shape because it keeps uncertainty in the name. Harold's wording leaves out that we do not know what the figure was.

public_record.headline: Sam Evers proposes "Reservoir Road Tall" as name for reservoir animal
Harold Vale and Ellen Price dispute Sam Evers' proposed name
Reservoir animal naming debate draws community comment

turns.text: Sam, are you standing by the name you proposed?
Yes. It says what I could tell, and no more.
Harold, what troubles you about it?
It sounds like a label made from the first report. A useful name ought to be less hasty.
Useful to whom? We should at least agree whether a name describes a report or a thing.
I am naming what I saw, not claiming to know what it was.
That distinction is fair. I still think I can do better, but I will wait for the proper turn.
And I will reserve mine too. The minutes should say who proposed what, not merely who spoke longest.
There are no other nominations tonight.
Then I am content to leave mine on the record.
On the record, yes. Not necessarily on the sign.
There is no sign in evidence, Harold.
We have the three proposals on tonight's sheet. Sam, does the new list alter yours?
No. Reservoir Road Tall still seems honest about the limits of my view.
Harold, what makes your wording practical?
Roadside Figure is brief. A person can say it once without needing to consult the minutes.
Brevity is not the same as accuracy. Unidentified Tall Shape states what is missing.
It states it at length. I do not see why the uncertainty needs three words.
I can accept uncertainty. I only want the location left in the record.
The record can hold the location. The name need not pretend the report is a map.
For clarity, neither of you is speaking from personal sight of it.
Correct. I am judging the wording, not the sighting.
And I would like the proposals entered under their proposers, in that order.
Tonight's three proposals are still on the sheet. Sam, do you want the place kept in the name?
Yes. Reservoir Road Tall says where I was and what I could make out.
It says where your report came from. That is not quite the same as naming the thing.
Which is why Unidentified Tall Shape is more exact about what remains unknown.
I don't object to unknown. I object to losing the location.
Roadside Figure keeps it short, and it doesn't claim a conclusion.
It also removes the word tall, which is the one description we have from Sam.
A name is not an inventory. I would rather leave room for correction.
For the record, neither Harold nor Ellen reports seeing anything.
Correct. I am disputing the wording, not adding testimony.
Then keep all three proposals attributed properly. Mine stays mine.
They will remain listed under their respective proposers.
